summary: Specifies extensions to IKEv2 that let two endpoints signal Robust Header Compression channel parameters when setting up IPsec security associations. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: When two parties set up a secret tunnel, they also agree on shortcuts for writing the repeated parts.

subtitle: How two IPsec peers use IKEv2 to agree on Robust Header Compression settings for a Child SA.

tldr.problem: ROHC over IPsec needs configuration parameters set at the compressor and decompressor, but the usual way to negotiate them, a link-layer protocol such as PPP, does not fit IPsec peers.
tldr.mechanism: A new ROHC_SUPPORTED Notify payload in the IKE_AUTH and CREATE_CHILD_SA exchanges carries a list of ROHC attributes: MAX_CID, ROHC_PROFILE, ROHC_INTEG, and optionally ROHC_ICV_LEN and MRRU.
tldr.outcome: Each ROHC-enabled IPsec SA gets its own negotiated ROHC channel, and ROHC is not enabled if the responder does not answer. It is a Proposed Standard with no obsoleting RFC listed.

today: RFC 5857 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata for this site lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is meant to be read with RFC 5856 and RFC 5858.

sections.title: Why IKEv2 Needs a ROHC Extension
sections.content:
IPsec adds header overhead, which can waste bandwidth. Combining Robust Header Compression (ROHC) with IPsec is an efficient way to carry protected IP traffic. The compressor and decompressor in ROHCoIPsec need configuration parameters, and hop-by-hop ROHC normally negotiates them through a link-layer protocol such as PPP.

Since key exchange protocols such as IKEv2 already set up parameters dynamically between IPsec peers, this document defines IKEv2 extensions that signal the ROHC parameters instead.
sections.plainLanguage: IPsec makes every package a bit bigger. ROHC shrinks the repeated labels. This RFC gives the two computers a way to agree on the shrinking rules while they set up their tunnel.

sections.title: The ROHC_SUPPORTED Notify Message
sections.content:
ROHC channel parameters MUST be signaled separately for each ROHC-enabled IPsec SA. A new Notify message type, ROHC_SUPPORTED, MUST be included in the IKE_AUTH and CREATE_CHILD_SA exchanges whenever a new ROHC-enabled IPsec SA is created or an existing one is rekeyed.

The initiator's Notify payload MUST carry the channel parameters, describing the capabilities of the ROHC decompressor at the initiator. The responder either ignores the payload (if it does not support ROHC or the proposed parameters) or answers with a Notify payload holding its own parameters.

Only one Notify payload carries ROHC parameters. If several arrive, all but the first MUST be dropped. If the initiator never receives the responder's parameters, ROHC MUST NOT be enabled on the Child SA.

Most parameters are one-way notifications: the sender says what it can handle, so each direction may announce different values.
sections.plainLanguage: One computer asks, "Can we use the shorthand? Here is what I can read." If the other one does not answer with its own list, they do not use shorthand at all.

sections.title: Payload and Attribute Formats
sections.content:
The Notify payload is the one defined in RFC 4306, with these settings: the Critical bit MUST be zero, the Protocol ID MUST be zero, the SPI Size MUST be zero (so no SPI field is sent), and the Notify Message Type MUST be ROHC_SUPPORTED. The Notification Data MUST contain at least three ROHC Attributes.

Each ROHC Attribute is modeled on the IKEv2 Transform Attributes. It starts with an Attribute Format (AF) bit and a 15-bit attribute type. If AF is 0 the attribute is Type/Length/Value, with a 2-octet length. If AF is 1 it is Type/Value, and the value is always 2 octets with no length field.
sections.plainLanguage: Each setting is a small labeled note. Short notes have the label and a two-byte value. Longer ones also say how long they are.

sections.title: The Five ROHC Attributes
sections.content:
MAX_CID is mandatory, sent exactly once. It is the largest context identifier the decompressor supports, from 0 to 16383, so the number of usable contexts is MAX_CID+1. The recipient MUST NOT use larger context identifiers.

ROHC_PROFILE is mandatory, with at least one sent. Each holds a 2-octet profile identifier and the recipient MUST use only the proposed profiles. Two versions of the same profile MUST NOT both be signaled, for example ROHCv1 UDP (0x0002) and ROHCv2 UDP (0x0102), because compressed packets carry only the 8 least-significant bits of the profile identifier, which are identical for the two.

ROHC_INTEG is mandatory, with at least one sent. It names the integrity algorithm used to check that decompressed headers match the originals. The responder MUST pick exactly one proposed algorithm, which is used in both directions; if none is acceptable, ROHC MUST NOT be enabled. A value of zero means NONE, in which case no integrity algorithm is applied. Keys come from the IKEv2 KEYMAT, and ROHC is treated as an IPsec protocol for that derivation.

ROHC_ICV_LEN is optional (zero or one). It gives the number of ICV octets the sender expects on incoming ROHC packets, and the ICV is truncated to that many bytes. Zero means no ICV is sent; a missing or too-large value means the full ICV is sent.

MRRU is optional (zero or one) and 2 octets long. It is the size of the largest reconstructed unit the decompressor will reassemble from ROHC segments, including the CRC and ROHC ICV. If it is 0 or absent, segment headers MUST NOT be sent. Unknown attribute types MUST be silently ignored.
sections.plainLanguage: The note lists how many conversations the reader can keep track of, which shorthand styles it knows, how to double-check the result, how long the checksum should be, and how big a reassembled message may be.

sections.title: Parameters That Must Not Be Signaled
sections.content: Two ROHC channel parameters are set implicitly and MUST NOT be signaled. LARGE_CIDS follows from MAX_CID: if MAX_CID is 15 or less, it is assumed to be 0. FEEDBACK_FOR is set to the other SA of the pair, the one pointing in the reverse direction, whenever a pair of SAs is created.
sections.plainLanguage: Some settings can be worked out from others, so the computers do not send them at all.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
Being able to negotiate the ROHC ICV length may introduce vulnerabilities. A short ICV can let erroneous packets be forwarded into the protected domain. Using longer ICVs mitigates this, at the cost of overhead that reduces the benefit of ROHCoIPsec. The details are in RFC 5856 and RFC 5858.

IANA allocated one value from the "IKEv2 Notify Message Types" registry for ROHC_SUPPORTED and created a "ROHC Attribute Types" registry. Values 1 to 5 are MAX_CID, ROHC_PROFILE, ROHC_INTEG, ROHC_ICV_LEN and MRRU, 0 is reserved, 6 to 16383 are unassigned, and 16384 to 32767 are for private use. New values need Expert Review.
sections.plainLanguage: A very short checksum is easier to fool. Using a longer one is safer but makes messages bigger again.
